The two male Groomers working there today should absolutely be fired for their horrible customer service treatment.

I am writing to formally complain about an experience I had during my second appointment at the Petco location in the Sepulveda/Burbank area.

During my first appointment, I arrived with my two cats using the same carriers/restraints and following the safety procedures I understood Petco required. On that occasion, I was treated respectfully, and the staff was kind and helpful. I had no issues whatsoever.

During my second appointment, I arrived with my two cats separated and secured, just as I had done during my first visit. However, the employee assisting me told me that my cats could not be seen unless I placed them inside a cardboard box. I did not refuse to cooperate or refuse to follow instructions. My concern was that the cardboard box did not provide the same level of safety and security for my cats as the carriers I had brought with me.

I was also instructed to move my cats into the cardboard box outside the store, despite the fact that the weather conditions were extremely hot. As a pet owner, I was very concerned about exposing my cats to high temperatures while handling them outside in an unsecured cardboard box. I was trying to protect my animals and avoid putting them at unnecessary risk.

What was especially upsetting was the inconsistency between my two visits. During my first appointment, I followed the same type of safety precautions and was treated very well. During my second appointment, I was treated very differently despite arriving prepared and making a genuine effort to comply with the instructions given to me.

If I could give zero stars, I would. This was by far the worst experience I’ve ever had with Petco.
I was taken aback by the complete lack of courtesy, consideration, or basic customer service at the Petco location on Sepulveda (Store #5850, Van Nuys). I purchased a fish that was clearly already sick and stressed at the time of sale. Within hours of bringing it home, it showed signs of illness and eventually infected my entire, well-established tank—putting my previously healthy fish at risk.
When I returned to the store requesting an exchange or refund, I was met with dismissive and rude behavior from the associates. This was especially frustrating considering the store itself has multiple fish currently under observation and not for sale due to illness and rapid decline—clearly indicating an ongoing issue with their fish stock.
While I did unfortunately misplace my receipt, my purchase was fully verifiable through my phone number and Petco account history, which clearly shows the fish was purchased just three days prior. Despite this, the associates made every excuse possible to deny any form of resolution or goodwill.
The fish ultimately passed away, which was upsetting enough on its own. Waking up to see my existing fish displaying the same symptoms made the situation even worse. I’m now at a loss not only for the fish I purchased, but potentially my entire tank due to a preventable issue.
This experience was extremely disappointing and stressful. I have filed a formal complaint and hope Petco takes this seriously, as no customer should be treated this way—especially when the issue stems from selling sick animals. I sincerely hope others do not have to go through a similar experience.Also the names of the associates are sevyn and Jesus that work in the evening shift

The second time, I came to buy a guinea pig. I had everything required for proper care: a large cage, food, and all necessary supplies. Despite that, I was refused the sale. The supervisor gave many excuses, and I left feeling very upset. My child was also very disappointed.

After that, I went to another store where I was able to purchase a guinea pig without any issues and received great customer service — they actually helped me.
